items.summary:
Google has introduced the Pixel Watch 5, featuring Gemini Intelligence for hands-free, proactive assistance and enhanced health tracking capabilities. The watch offers the most accurate GPS tracking yet and new Health Guardian features such as breathing emergency detection and monthly wellness summaries for blood pressure, sleep, and metabolic health. Pre-orders began on August 12, with general availability starting August 20.

The Pixel Watch 5 is powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 processor with increased RAM and CPU speed, enabling faster and more responsive AI interactions. It includes improvements like At a Glance dynamic updates, Raise to Talk enhancements, and one-handed gesture controls for seamless user experience. The device leverages advanced environmental modeling and real-time atmospheric data to deliver precise location tracking even in challenging urban and trail environments.

These upgrades build on the previous Pixel Watch model's foundation, aiming to provide users with timely, context-aware assistance and comprehensive health monitoring to help manage daily tasks and fitness more effectively.

The update includes improved safety measures calibrated to the model's expanded capabilities, supporting use cases such as vulnerability patching and engineering design acceleration. Pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, with a fast variant available at double the price. Users receive double included usage in Grok Build and Cursor during the first week of release.

items.originalTitle: Someone is running mass vulnerability scans, spoofing AI bots like ClaudeBot
items.summary:
A recent analysis reveals that mass vulnerability scans are being conducted by actors spoofing the identities of AI bots such as ClaudeBot. This spoofing involves impersonating recognized AI agents without proper authentication, potentially bypassing security measures that rely on bot identification.

The activity is part of a broader trend where the internet is increasingly accessed and reshaped by AI agents, crawlers, and bots, which affects how information is discovered and used. The report highlights the challenges in distinguishing legitimate AI traffic from malicious scans, emphasizing the need for improved verification methods to protect websites from spoofed bot traffic.

items.title: Discovered Materials launches AI agents to identify new thermally conductive dielectric materials for 3D chip packaging, releasing over 500 novel candidates with synthesis challenges [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Launch HN: Discovered Materials (YC P26) – AI agents to discover new materials
items.summary:
Discovered Materials has introduced AI agents designed to discover new materials for the semiconductor industry, focusing on thermally conductive dielectric materials to enable 3D chip packaging and improve energy efficiency. The project has identified over 500 previously unknown materials that meet multiple performance criteria, but only one has a plausible synthesis pathway for experimental production so far.

The AI models tested include GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude Fable, Claude Opus, and Kimi K3, with GPT-5.6-Sol discovering the most viable materials and producing the only experimentally plausible synthesis recipe. However, most synthesis proposals were critically flawed, highlighting the difficulty of translating computational discoveries into practical lab synthesis. The initiative aims to continue refining these methods and experimentally validate AI-designed materials to advance semiconductor technology.

items.title: Google DeepMind launches SL2T, a multilingual sign-language-to-text AI model powering sign-to-text features on Pixel 11 and Gboard starting with ASL [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Putting sign language AI into usersâ hands
items.summary:
Google DeepMind introduced SL2T, a sign-language-to-text translation model trained on over 100,000 hours across 50+ sign languages, enabling Deaf and hard of hearing users to sign to their phones for dictation and communication. The model powers new features in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11, starting with American Sign Language to English, with plans to expand to more devices and languages.

SL2T processes sign language as sequences of body pose landmarks rather than raw video to protect privacy, translating these directly into text without relying on intermediate gloss annotations. This approach addresses the complexity of sign languages, which involve simultaneous movements and distinct grammars, and outperforms single-language models by leveraging multilingual training. The technology aims to improve accessibility and bridge communication gaps between Deaf and hearing communities.

items.originalTitle: Gemini API removes postpay billing
items.summary:
Google announced that starting September 14, 2026, developers using paid features of the Gemini API in AI Studio must switch their billing plan from postpay to prepay. This change aims to give developers more control over API consumption and costs and applies only to Gemini API usage within AI Studio, while other Google Cloud Platform services remain on postpay.

Developers are advised to transition to the prepay billing plan and purchase credits before the deadline to avoid service interruptions. Google also recommends configuring auto-reload to maintain prepaid balances and ensure continuous access to paid Gemini API features.

items.title: Report: Legacy data systems limit AI agent scaling and decision speed; data leaders overcome constraints with broader data access and trust in agent decisions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
items.summary:
A new report based on a survey of 300 data and technology executives finds that many organizations struggle to realize the full potential of agentic AI due to inadequate infrastructure and limited access to enterprise data. While AI agents require broad, real-time access to structured and unstructured data across operational systems, legacy data systems often create bottlenecks that restrict AI effectiveness and scaling.

The report highlights a group of "data leaders" who provide AI agents access to over 70% of their data and report higher trust in AI decisions, enabling faster and more scalable AI deployment. In contrast, "data laggards" typically grant access to 30% or less of their data and face significant limitations from legacy systems. With predictions that AI agents will influence or automate half of business decisions by 2027, organizations face increasing pressure to modernize data estates to support agentic AI at scale.

In the past two weeks, Nvidia stock has risen 18% and Apple’s has fallen 10% or so. We got a reminder about the frothiness of demand for AI capacity right now from executives at two small Nvidia-backed cloud firms, CoreWeave and Nebius, speaking on earnings calls in the past two days. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh revealed today that Nebius had held its first auction of computing capacity during the second quarter, with prices for Nvidia’s Blackwell generation of chips “15% above the highest price we ever charged before.” Volozh also said Nebius was selling more capacity closer to the time customers needed it to take advantage of high prices.
